0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 26 October 1988, after the draft finalized by the Electrical Insulators and Accessories Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. 0.2 This standard has been revised in the light of experience gained in the manufacture and use of porcelain bushings in the country. The following changes have been incorporated in this revision: a) The bushing been added, of 800 A current and rating has

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements, characteristics and methods of tests for porcelain bushings for indoor and outdoor use, suitable for electrical equipment of nominal system voltages up to and including 1 000 V and frequency between 15 and 60 Hz. 1.2 This standard also applies to bushings supplied separately for use in the construction of electrical apparatus, transformers, electrical installations and to bushings supplied as an integral part of equipment when required by the relevant equipment specifications. 1.3 This standard does not apply to bushings for use with rectifiers, rotating machines, testing transformers, dc converter transformers or to terminal?, for power cables ( pot heads ). Such

bushings, if not covered by relevant Indian Standard, shall 6e subjected to special agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of ~this standard, the following definitions, in addition to those covered in IS : 2099-1986* and IS : I885 ( Part 54 )-19807 shall apply 2.1 Bushings - A structure carrying one or several conductors through a partition, such as, a wall or tank, etc, and insulating it or them therefrom, incorporating the means of attachment ( flange or othe.r fixing device ) to the partition.

NOTE l-

The rated current of the bushing need not with the rated current of necessarily be identical the complete apparatus. It may be higher or lower, depending upon how t& actual service conditions deviate from the standard test conditions for the bushing. The general rule for the permissible service current should be such that it shall not give rise to higher actual conductor temperatures than the temperature-rise permitted in 7, added to the temperature of the relevant cooling medium.

5.3 Rated Thermal Short Time Current ( Ith ) 5.3.1 Unless otherwise stated, the rated duration ( tth ) shall be 1 second except for transformer bushings. The transformer bushings shall be rated for 2 seconds.
5.3.2 Minimum Values IJnless otherwise stated, the minimum value of rated short time current of a bushing is 25 times the rated current for the rated duration.
NOTE - Experience has shown that if a bushing is -correctly designed for its rated current, it is not generally necessary to prove, by test, its thermal and mechanical performance under a short time current loading of 25 times the rated current for one second. If, exceptionally, a higher short time current is required, the need for a test should be decided by agreement between the purchaser and the supplier.

These conditions will replace those specified above when the corresponding test voltage values and correction factors are available.
NOTE 3 - Except by agreement between the manufacturer and purchaser, tests shall not be made if the relative humidity exceeds 85 percent. No-4 - Corrections of test voltage for atmos: pheric conditions differing from 3.1 shall be applied in accordance with Appendix A.

4. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 4.1 The porcelain shall be sound,

5.4 Rated Frequency - The value of frequency of the bushings may be any between 15 and 60 Hz.

rated value

free from defects, thoroughly vitrified and smoothly glazed and shall comply with the appropriate class given in IS : 5621-19807. 4.2 The design of the bushing shall be such that the stress due to expansion or contraction in any part of the bushing shall not lead to deterioration. 4.3 The glaze, unless otherwise specified, shall be brown in colour. The glaze shall cover all the

exposed porcelain parts of the bushing except those areas which serve as supports during firing or required to be left unglazed. 4.4 All the ferrous metal parts except the threads of the nuts shall be hot-dip galvanized. The threads of the nuts shall be cut after galvanization.

Rated thermal short time current withstand test ( 11.9 ), Pressure test on liquid filled and liquid insulated bushings ( 11.10 ), and Tightness test at the flange or other fixing device ( 11.11).
NOTE 1 - Type tests are normally made once and unless otherwise agreed to, the test certificate giving the results of type tests made on not less than two bushings identical in all essential details with those to be supplied are regarded as evidence of compliance. -Both the bushings shall be subjected to tests ( a ) to ( f ), after which one shall be subjected to test ( g ) and the other to test (h ). 9. MARKING 9.1 Each bushing shall be legibly

and indelibly marked to show the following: a) Name or trade-mark of the manufacturer, b) Year of_manufacture, and c) Country of manufacture.

9.1.1 Marking on porcelain shall be printed and shall be applied before firing. 9.1.2 The porcelain bushings may also be marked with the Standard Mark.
NOTE - The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereThe Standard Mark on products covered by under. an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that Standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the Standard marked products are also producer. continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions -under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may he obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards

11.1.2 Acceptance Tests - The test Samples after`having withstood the routine tests shall be subjected to the following acceptance tests in the order indicated below: a) Verification of dimensions ( 11.3 ), b) Dry power-frequency voltage withstand test ( 11.4 ), c) Temperature cycle test ( 11.6 ), d) Porosity test ( 11.7 ), e) Pressure test on liquid filled and liquid insulated bushings ( ll.lO), and f) Tightness test at the flange or other fixing device ( 11.11 ). 11.1.2.1 For carrying out acceptance tests specified in this standard, the sampling procedure and the criterion of conformity to the requirements of acceptance tests shall be as given in Appendix B. 11.1.3 Routine Tests - The following tests shall constitute routine tests: a) Visual examination ( 11.2 ), b) Voltage test ( 11.4 and 11.5 ), c) Pressure test on liquid filled and liquid insulated bushings ( 11.10 >, and d) Tightness t&t at the flange or other fixing device ( 11.11). 11.2 Visual

11.6.1 The porcelain parts of the bushings shall be quickly and completely immersed in a water bath maintained at a temperature of 70�C above-that of the cold water and left submerged for a period of 15 minutes. It shall then be withdrawn and quickly immersed completely without being placed in an intermediate container, in a bath of cold water for the same period of 15 minutes. 11.6.2 This heating and cooling cycle shall performed three times in+succession. be

11.4.1 The bushing shall be tested dry under the conditions prescribed in Appendix C. 11.4.2 The voltage given atmospheric in Appendix bushings shall be subjected to test in 8.1 ( subject to adjustment for conditions at the time of test given A ) for a period of one minute.

11.6.3 After the completion of the immersion, the bushings shall be examined to verify that the bushing parts have not cracked and that the glaze is undamaged. 11.7 Porosity Test

11.4.3 A test voltage of about 7.5 percent of the specified voltage as determined in 11.4.2 shall be applied and then increased gradually to reach the specified test voltage in a time not less than five seconds. Flashover or puncture shall not occur [ see IS : 2071 ( Part 1 )-1974* ] -after the application of the voltage for one minute. 11.5 Wet Power-Frequency Test ( for Outdoor Bushings Voltage ) Withstand

11.7.1 Porcelain fragments from the bushings shall be immersed in orie percent alcoholic solution of fuchsin ( 1 g fuchsin in 100 g of methylated spirit ) under a pressure of not less than 15 x 10"iU/m2 for a period such that the product of test duration in hours and test pressure in N/m" is not less than 180 X 10s. 11.7.2 The fragments shall then be removed from the solution, washed,~dried and broken. 11.7.3 Examination with naked eye of the freshly broken surface shall not reveal any dye penetration. Penetration into small cracks rormed during the initial breaking shall be neglected. 11.8 Temperature-Rise Test

11.10.1 Test with Oil or Insulating Liquid at Ambient Temperature - The bushing complete as for normal service shall be filled to the normal level with oil or insulating liquid of the quality specified by the manufacturer. The bushings shall be placed in air at ambient temperature of not less than 10�C. The temperature of the oil or insulating liquid shall be the ambient temperature. The following test pressure shall be produced inside the bushings and maintained for at least 12 hours: a) For bushings operating at a pressure above the attiospheric pressure between 0'6 and 2 bar b) For bushings operating at a pressure above the atmospheric pressure between 0 and 0'6 bar To be tested at a pressure of 1'0 f 0'1 bar above the maximum operating pressure To be tested at a pressure of 1'0 f. 0'1 bar above the ~atmospheric pressure to be effecof leakage

11.11.1 The test shall be .aQplicable to all bushings of indoor-immersed, outdoor-immersed and completely immersed types, intended to -be used as an integral part of an apparatus, such as switchgear or transformer, where the bushings contribute to the sealing of the complete apparatus. 11.11.2 The bushing shall be assembled as far as necessary for the test. The end for immersion shall be mounted on a tank as for normal operation. The tank shall be filled with air and any suitable gas at a gauge pressure of 1'5 f 0'1 bar and maintained for 15 minutes. 11.11.3 The bushing shall have passed the test if there leakage. be considered is no evidence to of

HUMIDITY CORRECTION FACTOR

Locate the point corresponding to the deviation of the ambient atmospheric (pressure from 1 013 millibars on the left hand side of Fig. 2B and join it with right hand side top `corner by a straight line. Then locate the point on the curve in Fig. 2A corresponding to the observed value of the difference of dry and wet bulb temperature. Draw a vertical line through this point to intersect the straight line drawn in Fig. 2B. Read the correction to be applied to humidity from the right hand side of Fig. 2B corresponding to the point of intersection. This correction is positive for a positive deviation and negative for negative deviation from the standard atmospheric pressure.

HIGH C-l. ARRANGEMENT C-l.1 The bushing OF BUSHING VOLTAGE TESTS
unless flange. otherwise stated, the earthed fixing

shall be clean and dry.

C-l.2 -High voltage tests shall be carried out only on bushings eomplete with their fixing flanges or other fixing devices and all other accessories with which they are fitted when in use but with protective gap, if any, removed. C-l.3 For bushings intended for immersion, the immersed end of a bushing designed to function in an insulating medium, shall be immersed to the immersion level of the bushing except that where there is earthed metal extending to this level, the depth of immersion may be increased Bushings shall be tested up to the fixing flange. in the medium in which they are intended to function in service or, by agreement, in oil complying with IS : 335-1983". The insulating medium shall be at room temperature. Bushings need not be immersed in oil when their dimensions permit the tests to be made in air. C-2.1 Power-frequency'tests shall be made accordance with IS : 2071 ( Part 1 )-1974*.

C-2.1.1 The transformer test circuit shall be such that when the test object i's short-circuited at the test voltage, the current is not less than 0'1.4 if~dry tests are to be made, and not less than 0'5A if the wet tests are to be made. C-3. EXCESSIVE HUMIDITY C-3.1 Precautions shall be taken to avoid condensation on the surface of the bushing, specially when the relative humidity is high. For example, the bushing shall be maintained at the ambient temperature of the test location for sufficient time for equilibrium to be reached before the Except by agreement between test commences. the manufacturer and the purchaser, tests shall not be made if the relative humidity exceeds 85 percent.
